acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Given `gaia-validate-feature-docs`'s worker schema no longer requires `needsRequirementsFix`/`needsTechSpecFix`, when a response's JSON candidate omits both fields but includes `valid`/`findings`/`report`, then `extractDelimitedStructuredOutput` recovers it on the first attempt

Given a response's JSON candidate DOES include `needsRequirementsFix`/`needsTechSpecFix` with the correct boolean type, when `worker()` processes that attempt, then behavior is unchanged from today — the fields are still validated when present

Given a schema-required worker's attempt ends in free text with no recoverable structured output even after the relaxed schema, when `worker()` processes that attempt, then the next attempt (bounded by `WORKER_MAX_ATTEMPTS`) retries with a corrective nudge appended to the prompt

Given every attempt exhausts `WORKER_MAX_ATTEMPTS` still without usable structured output, when `worker()` finishes its attempt loop, then the existing `"Worker returned no structured output"` error is thrown

Given `req/index.md`'s Acceptance Criteria table has first 3 columns other than exactly `ID`, `Criterion`, `Related UC` in order, when `req-skeleton-check.js` runs, then it fails immediately with a precise column-shape error, never reaching `parseAcTable`'s positional destructure
Given `req/index.md`'s Acceptance Criteria table has the correct 4-column header, when `req-skeleton-check.js` runs, then behavior is unchanged from today
Given `gaia-generate-requirements.md`'s own inline AC example, when inspected, then it matches the real, authoritative 4-column template, no longer a stale 3-column duplicate

Given a non-schema worker's response has a whole-response fence wrap that opens but never closes, with a real heading after the opener, when `extractMarkdownDocument` processes it, then the opener is stripped and the remainder (containing the real heading) is returned
Given a non-schema worker's response has a CLOSED whole-response fence wrap, when `extractMarkdownDocument` processes it, then behavior is unchanged from today

Given a per-component generation result fails `isValidComponentDetail` on its first attempt but passes on an immediate retry, when `pm-phase1.js`'s per-component loop runs, then the retried result is written and no error surfaces

Given a per-component generation result fails `isValidComponentDetail` on both attempts, when `pm-phase1.js`'s per-component loop runs, then the loop throws immediately, naming the specific component, before any later component is dispatched

Given a per-UC generation result fails `isValidUseCaseFile` on both attempts, when `pm-phase1.js`'s per-UC loop runs, then the loop throws immediately, naming the specific UC, before any later UC is dispatched
Given all changes are delivered, when `npm test` runs, then all tests pass: new regression tests for AC-01 through AC-12, and a full-suite regression
